new.name: Feather Game Changer
new.description: The Game Changer built with feathers: short gold brush sections on each shank veiled with hen cape feathers, a pheasant rump tail and synthetic jungle cock eyes. Lighter than the chenille version and very lifelike.
new.fishing_tips: Strip and pause; the feathers breathe on every stop. Great for trout, bass and smallmouth.
mats: Short dubbing or fly brush sections (1in and 3in)
Hen cape feathers, a pair per section
steps: Tie a pheasant rump tail on the tail shank, wrap a turn of brush and tie a pair of hen feathers flat each side as a veil.
Link the next shank, wrap a slightly longer brush section and veil it with slightly bigger feathers so each section overlaps the one behind.
Repeat up the shanks to the hook, growing each section a little.
Finish with the fullest brush section on the hook, trim the head to a baitfish taper and comb the fibres back.
Glue on the eyes, add a drop of resin at the head and whip finish.

tutorial_links.label: Feather Game Changer recipe and photos (Mad River Outfitters blog)

new.name: Polar Changer
new.description: Chocklett's Polar Fiber Game Changer: each shank is hollow-tied with small bundles of Polar Fiber, a long, translucent synthetic that sheds water, so a big fly still casts easily.
new.fishing_tips: A great size-for-weight streamer for big bass, pike and stripers. Strip it hard and let it glide.
mats: Polar Fiber, white with darker colour on top
A few strands of flash per section
steps: Tie a small Polar Fiber tail on the hook, hollow-tie style (tie it in around the shank and fold it back).
Link the hook to the smallest shank and hollow-tie a bundle on it, slightly longer than the one behind.
Repeat up each shank, adding a few flash strands and darker fibre on top for a back.
Build the biggest, fullest bundles on the front shank to make the head.
Trim lightly to a tapered profile, colour with markers and glue on the eyes.

new.name: Finesse Changer
new.description: A slimmer, lighter Game Changer made with Chocklett's Finesse Body Chenille. Its narrow profile swims at slower retrieves and gets eaten by wary fish.
new.fishing_tips: Use it when fish follow a full Game Changer but won't commit; fish it slower and on lighter rods.
mats: Craft fur or a few synthetic fibres
Chocklett's Finesse Body Chenille, medium and large
steps: Tie a small tail on the hook and wrap medium Finesse chenille, stroking the fibres back.
Link the hook to a short shank and wrap a slightly fuller section.
Continue up the shanks, switching to large chenille on the front sections.
Trim to a slim, narrow baitfish shape; keep it thin from above so it swims at slow speeds.
Colour the back, glue on the eyes and whip finish.

tutorial_links.label: Finesse Game Changer (Fly Fishing the Ozarks)

new.name: Crafty Changer
new.description: A two-hook Game Changer variant with a feather flicker tail, a cut shank connection, a rattle and a stacked craft fur head with pectoral fins.
new.fishing_tips: Strip and pause; the craft fur head pushes water and the rattle helps in stained water.
mats: Kona BGH, Ahrex Minnow or Gamakatsu SL12S
Cactus or Filler flash with feather flicker tail
steps: On the rear hook tie the flash and feather tail and a hen collar.
Join the rear hook to the front hook with a cut 25mm shank.
Lash a rattle on the front hook.
Tie in pectoral fins each side.
Stack two bunches of craft fur for the head, trim to shape, glue on the eyes.

new.name: Bugger Changer
new.description: A Woolly Bugger built on micro spines: a marabou tail with hackle, then several jointed sections of streamer brush palmered with hen saddle, and dumbbell eyes so it jigs.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it like a bugger with more kick: strip, pause and let it drop.
mats: Mini marabou, black, with a hen saddle hackle
Streamer brush with hen saddle palmered
steps: Tie a marabou tail on the hook and palmer a little hen saddle.
Link the hook to the first spine and wrap a section of brush and hackle.
Repeat on each spine.
Tie dumbbell eyes on the front spine, wrap a brush head around them and whip finish.

new.name: Micro Changer
new.description: A tiny Game Changer on micro shanks for trout, panfish and small bass; the same swimming action scaled down to minnow and fry size.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it on a 5–6 weight with short strips; deadly when fish key on small baitfish.
steps: Tie a tiny tail and a few turns of chenille on the hook.
Link it to the first micro shank and wrap a slightly fuller section.
Repeat up three or four shanks.
Trim to a small minnow shape, colour it and add the eyes.

tutorial_links.label: Mini Feather Jerk Changer (Mad River Outfitters)

new.name: T-Bone
new.description: Chocklett's big musky and pike fly: a long, articulated body with a bulky head that pushes water, built for figure-eights at the boat.
new.fishing_tips: Use a heavy sinking-tip line and a wire bite tippet; work it with long sweeping strips and finish every cast with a figure-eight.
mats: Long synthetic fibres or bucktail with flash
Chocklett's Body Tubing or large brush
Bucktail or a sculpting brush, trimmed full
steps: Tie a long tail with flash on the rear hook.
Link the shanks to the rear hook with bite wire.
Cover the shanks with body tubing or brush for a long, flexing body.
Join the front hook and build a full head that will push water.
Trim the head, glue on big eyes and coat the head with flexible resin.

new.name: Hybrid Changer
new.description: Chocklett's hybrid: a rear hook and front hook joined by a shank, with a rattle, hen pectoral fins and a sculpted brush head. It mixes Game Changer swimming with the profile of a classic articulated streamer.
new.fishing_tips: A top fly for big predators. Strip hard and pause; the head makes it dart and the rattle calls fish in.
steps: Dress the rear hook with a tail and a short body.
Join it to the front hook with a shank and wire.
Lash a rattle under the front shank.
Tie in hen pectoral fins each side.
Wrap a sculpting brush head, trim it to shape and add the eyes.

tutorial_links.label: Building a blended Hybrid Game Changer (Dirty Water)

new.name: Jerk Changer
new.description: A Game Changer with a head shaped so the fly darts side to side on a jerk retrieve, like a jerkbait: shanks, a hen hackle tail and a Chocklett chenille body.
new.fishing_tips: Fish it with sharp, short rod-tip twitches, not long strips: the fly snaps left and right.
steps: Tie a hen hackle tail on the hook and wrap chenille.
Link the shanks one at a time, wrapping chenille on each.
On the front shank make a flat-sided head; this shape is what makes it dart.
Trim, colour and add the eyes.

tutorial_links.label: Game Changers vs Jerk Changers explained (Mad River Outfitters)

new.name: Bucktail Game Changer
new.description: A big, light Game Changer for pike and musky: each section is hollow-tied with bucktail so the fly breathes, pushes water and still casts.
new.fishing_tips: Use heavy wire tippet and long strips with figure-eights at the boat.
steps: Hollow-tie a bunch of bucktail on the rear hook.
Link a shank with bite wire and hollow-tie a slightly bigger bunch with flash.
Repeat on each shank, growing the bunches.
Finish with the fullest bunches on the front hook for the head, glue on the eyes and coat the head.
